decisions.reason: As a core rye bread closely using existing recipes, skills and channels, it is unlikely to be cut absent any clear sign that its performance falls below aspiration levels.
The premium raisin stollen is a declared flagship and its gold-medal recognition gives management a strong above-aspiration signal, so it should clearly remain.
This seeded rye mixed bread fits the established assortment well and can be carried with little extra strain, so boundedly rational management would likely continue it while results become clearer.

The dark barley malt rye bread is somewhat more niche and overlaps with other rye products, but in a growing market the firm likely keeps it unless sales visibly disappoint relative to comparable breads.
The marzipan Christmas stollen is close to the firm’s seasonal strengths, and without evidence of a shortfall management would likely retain it as part of the holiday range.
Ancient grain bread is the most experimental of the group, yet it still builds on existing baking capabilities and available slack makes continued trial more likely than immediate withdrawal.
